summary: Virtual Path MES (Java Spring Cloud + Vue 3 + .NET 8 MQTT gateway + GLM-4 AI assistant, 646 commits, last commit 2026-08-24) has no tenancy anywhere, an OEE with upper-only clamping and unguarded null unboxing, an unscoped AI conversation API, and no Temporal, Rust, or Claude, so it is a weak reference for GreyHook's multi-tenant, read-only, ISO 22400 design.

d1_oee.formula: availability = runTime/(runTime+downtime); performance = idealCycleTime*totalProducts/runTime; quality = goodProducts/totalProducts; oee = A*P*Q; each factor capped with Math.min(x,1.0) and rounded to 2 dp (mes-dashboard/src/main/java/com/mes/dashboard/service/impl/DashboardServiceImpl.java lines 137-185)
d1_oee.storage: MySQL table dash_oee_data via MyBatis-Plus (mes-dashboard/src/main/java/com/mes/dashboard/entity/OeeData.java, OeeDataMapper.java); InfluxDB 2.x holds only device_telemetry, not OEE
gaps: Clamp is upper-bound only (DashboardServiceImpl.java lines 174-176); no lower bound, so negative runTime, downtime or counts yield negative or out-of-range OEE
Unchecked unboxing: downtime (Long) at line 168 and goodProducts (Integer) at line 172 have no null guard; only runTime and totalProducts are checked (lines 159-160)
Query is by deviceId only with LIMIT 1; OeeData has a dateHour column but no time window is applied, so there is no shift, day or hour granularity
calculateOee returns a computed object and never persists it; no insert or update path for dash_oee_data was found
No ISO 22400 reference in the OEE code; performance uses a single idealCycleTime * totalProducts / runTime with no per-product cycle model
OEE is per device with no organization scoping, consistent with the absence of tenancy

d2_downtime.model: Current-state row only: dash_device_status is updated from the 'status' key of mes-device-data messages (KafkaDeviceDataConsumer.java updateDeviceStatus) and from mes-alarm-event status messages (KafkaAlarmEventConsumer.java line 87). Entering ALARM auto-creates an alarm and leaving it resolves all active alarms (KafkaDeviceDataConsumer.java handleAlarmTransition). Liveness is a Redis key device:online:{id} with 90 s TTL (mes-device-gateway/src/MesDeviceGateway/Services/DeviceHeartbeatService.cs, GatewayConfig.cs).
schema_fields: Kafka mes-device-data value (DeviceDataMessage.cs): DeviceId, Timestamp (DateTime, UTC), Data (Dictionary of string to object, includes status), DataType; key = DeviceId
Kafka mes-alarm-event value (DeviceStatusMessage.cs): DeviceId, Status, HeartbeatTime, ExtraInfo
dash_device_status columns: deviceCode, deviceName, deviceType, status, temperature, speed, lastHeartbeat, workstationId, productionLineId, plus BaseEntity id/create/update/deleted fields
No state-transition event table; alarm rows are the only event history
gaps: No running/idle/fault/offline state model: status is a free string with values ONLINE/OFFLINE/ALARM
No state history or duration tracking, so downtime is not derived from state transitions; OEE downtime is an input column in dash_oee_data
Kafka producer uses Acks.Leader and EnableIdempotence = false; Java consumers do updateById plus an InfluxDB write per message with no dedup key, so redelivery double-counts
dash_device_status has no organization_id column

d3_device.edge_arch: mes-device-gateway (.NET 8 worker): MqttConsumerService subscribes to mes/device/+/data and mes/device/+/status, pushes messages into an in-process channel, DataCleanseService validates, filters abnormal values, deduplicates and runs a sliding window, then KafkaProducerService produces to mes-device-data or mes-alarm-event (Snappy, LingerMs 5). DeviceHeartbeatService writes heartbeats to Redis. Config in GatewayConfig.cs.
d3_device.write_guard: No device write-back path: the .NET gateway only subscribes (no MQTT publish calls found in any file read) and the AI tool layer has no device-control function. The only write tool is create_work_order, which targets the workorder service, not devices. Read-only by construction.
gaps: No EMQX-to-Kafka bridge configuration in the repo: docker-compose.yml only runs emqx:5.8.3 on port 1883; the .NET gateway performs the MQTT-to-Kafka hop in-process
MQTT is plaintext on 1883 by default with no TLS option in GatewayConfig.cs; MqttUsername and MqttPassword default to empty strings
No per-device authentication or topic ACL found; deviceId comes from the topic path, so any client able to publish can impersonate any device
EMQX dashboard default password falls back to 'public' (docker-compose.yml)
No OPC UA or other industrial protocol support found
Delivery is at-least-once with no idempotent producer and no consumer dedup key

d4_data_model.hierarchy: ProductionLine > Workstation > Device (dash_device_status carries productionLineId and workstationId); WorkOrder > ProcStep, ScheduleItem, WorkReport; BOM, Material, Inventory in mes-dashboard. No cross-service foreign-key contract or shared hierarchy table found.
d4_data_model.shift_model: mes_shift entity (mes-workorder/src/main/java/com/mes/workorder/entity/Shift.java): shiftCode DAY or NIGHT, startTime and endTime as LocalTime, isWork flag; WorkCalendarDay entity also exists. Shifts are not referenced by the OEE calculation or telemetry.
d4_data_model.telemetry_schema: InfluxDB measurement device_telemetry, tags device_code, fields temperature, speed, pressure, power, status, WritePrecision.S (mes-dashboard TelemetryServiceImpl.java). Kafka mes-device-data value is DeviceDataMessage {DeviceId, Timestamp, Data map, DataType}. No Timescale hypertable; InfluxDB 2.7 per README. MySQL for relational data.
d4_data_model.tenancy: None. BaseEntity (mes-common/src/main/java/com/mes/common/entity/BaseEntity.java) has id, createTime, updateTime, deleted, deletedTime, deletedBy only. sql/init.sql has zero organization, tenant or org_id columns. Cross-org 404 is not implemented.

d5_api.versioning: None. Gateway routes are /api/{service}/** with StripPrefix, with no /v1 segment. AI routes are /api/ai/** with StripPrefix=2.
d5_api.realtime: WebSocket at /api/ws/dashboard (mes-dashboard config/WebSocketConfig.java) with a SUBSCRIBE:<workstationId> text protocol (websocket/DashboardWebSocketHandler.java). setAllowedOriginPatterns('*'). No SSE found.
d5_api.envelope: mes-common Result<T> {code, message, data, timestamp}. AI service returns Pydantic response models without this wrapper.
d5_api.auth: Gateway JwtAuthGlobalFilter.java requires a Bearer JWT (401 otherwise) with whitelist /api/auth/login, /api/auth/register and /actuator/**. JwtUtils enforces HS256 secret of at least 32 bytes (JWT_SECRET). The WebSocket takes its JWT from the ?token= query string. The AI service re-verifies the JWT itself (mes-ai-service/src/security.py, HS256/384/512).

d6_ai.model: glm-4-flash (Zhipu GLM-4 family; FREE_MODELS whitelist in mes-ai-service/src/services/llm_service.py, temperature 0.7, max_tokens 1024). Not Claude.
gaps: 19 OpenAI-style function-calling tools (TOOL_DEFINITIONS in mes-ai-service/src/services/tools.py), not MCP
Not read-only: create_work_order (tools.py line 446-459) POSTs to the workorder service using the user's forwarded JWT
No tenant isolation: conversation and analysis APIs take user_id as a client query parameter defaulting to 'default'
Conversation GET/POST/DELETE look up by conv_id only with no owner check; client can write assistant messages into any conversation
Rate limit is one global Redis counter 'ratelimit:llm' (default 60/60s), not per user or tenant; does not cover the write tool separately
add_message accepts client-supplied role and steps, so client can inject assistant messages into any conversation

d7_quality.tests: JUnit: mes-common ResultTest.java and JwtUtilsTest.java. Vitest: mes-frontend auth.test.ts and markdown.test.ts. pytest: mes-ai-service/tests/test_prediction.py. No test files in mes-dashboard (including OEE), mes-gateway, mes-auth, mes-workorder, mes-process, mes-quality, or the .NET gateway.
d7_quality.ci: GitHub Actions .github/workflows/ci.yml on push/PR to develop and master. Build job: JDK 17 mvn clean package against MySQL 8.0.33, loads sql/init.sql, frontend npm ci, lint, vue-tsc type-check, vitest, vite build. Smoke job boots backend against MySQL and Redis; mes-dashboard excluded per CI comment. No pytest step and no .NET build or test step.
d7_quality.migrations: Manual numbered SQL in sql/ (V2 through V14, plus init.sql). No Flyway or Liquibase (only that pom was checked). CI loads only sql/init.sql. Duplicate version prefixes: V6__bom_inventory.sql and V6__seed_data.sql, V10 and V10_1, V5 and V5_5.
security_flags: AI conversation IDOR: get, add-message and delete by conv_id with no owner check
AI user_id is a client query parameter defaulting to 'default'
WebSocket JWT in ?token= query string plus wildcard origin patterns
Plaintext MQTT with empty default credentials (GatewayConfig.cs)
LLM can trigger create_work_order, a write action, from natural language
Gateway JwtAuthGlobalFilter does not consult the token blacklist; TokenBlacklistChecker exists only in mes-common (per-service use not verified)

adopt: Subscribe-only edge gateway with no publish path, matching GreyHook's outbound-only rule
Explicit work-order transition table via canTransitionTo (mes-workorder WorkOrderStatusEnum.java)
Alarm lifecycle driven by status transitions (KafkaDeviceDataConsumer.handleAlarmTransition)
Topic-derived device identity overriding payload identity, plus invalid-message drops (MqttConsumerService.cs, DataCleanseService.cs)
Redis heartbeat with TTL for liveness (DeviceHeartbeatService.cs)
Independent JWT verification in the AI service (security.py) and Redis INCR plus TTL rate limiting
Tool-call wrapper that normalizes errors and never raises into the orchestrator (tools.py _safe_request)
Backend smoke test booting services against real MySQL and Redis
avoid: Unscoped conversation endpoints with client-supplied user_id
Token in WebSocket query string with wildcard origins
OEE with upper-only clamp and unchecked unboxing
Actuator endpoints whitelisted at the gateway by default
Status events published to the alarm topic (mes-alarm-event) mixing semantics
Non-idempotent Kafka producer feeding non-deduplicating consumers
Single global LLM rate-limit counter instead of per-user/tenant
differentiate: Multi-tenancy: organization_id on every row with cross-org 404 (this repo has no tenant column anywhere)
ISO 22400 OEE with four machine states running/idle/fault/offline and [0,1] clamp (this repo uses ONLINE/OFFLINE/ALARM with upper-only clamp)
Read-only AI with claude-sonnet-4-6 and no write tools (this repo uses glm-4-flash and has create_work_order)
Temporal durable workflows (no Temporal anywhere in the tree)
TimescaleDB on PostgreSQL for telemetry (this repo uses InfluxDB 2.7 with MySQL for relational data)
